messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Hierarchies in Seemingly Unrelated Regressions?
parts:
Sorry for letting this one slip through the cracks. You (and
any other poster) should feel free to ping the list if we haven't
answered in a couple days. If things go this long, it's just that
we missed it.

A program should have a positive density (finite log density)
for any paramters satisfying the constraints.

One problem you have is here:

parameters {
vector <lower=-1, upper=1> [3] rho_sur;
vector <lower=0, upper=10> [3] sigma_sur;
...

transformed parameters{
cov_matrix[3] Sigma_sur;
Sigma_sur[1,1] <- square(sigma_sur[1]);
Sigma_sur[2,2] <- square(sigma_sur[2]);
Sigma_sur[3,3] <- square(sigma_sur[3]);
Sigma_sur[1,2] <- rho_sur[1]*sigma_sur[1]*sigma_sur[2];
Sigma_sur[1,3] <- rho_sur[2]*sigma_sur[1]*sigma_sur[3];
Sigma_sur[2,3] <- rho_sur[3]*sigma_sur[2]*sigma_sur[3];
Sigma_sur[2,1] <- Sigma_sur[1,2];
Sigma_sur[3,1] <- Sigma_sur[1,3];
Sigma_sur[3,2] <- Sigma_sur[2,3];


That's not a sound way to build a covariance matrix, because
there are values for rho for which Sigma_sur will not be positive
definite. You want to model the covariance matrix directly as
a parameter, or ideally use a Cholesky factor of a correlation
matrix and scale it.

Also, we don't generally recommend those interval-constrained priors
on scales --- we prefer <lower=0> and a weakly informative prior.

The program could also be sped up with more vectorization, but
I'd get it working first if it's not too slow already. One thing
you can do to speed things up is tighten some of the priros. Unless
g_a and g_b can take on values in the 100s, a normal(0, 100) isn't
reasonable.

- Bob





> On Mar 17, 2016, at 9:45 AM, Lindsay <lindsay...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear Stan Users,
>
> I am struggling with modelling hierarchies in a seemingly unrelated regressions model. I am aiming at a SUR version of something very like Example 17.2 in Gelman and Hill, but with the exception that instead of a single outcome variable I have three (by assumption) correlated outcome variables.
>
> The model I think I want to run is to be found in the attached file sur_mlm_1a. However, when I try to run it, although the model does compile and sample something goes wrong. For each of the parameters samples a single value (plus or minus a minimal amount of Monte Carlo error) rather than a distribution. Reading the discussion on this list (and having put in a query in the past) I am assuming that this may be a problem with the priors---a combination perhaps of having too tight a uniform prior, and also the fact that a uniform prior is perhaps not a great choice.
>
> After a hiatus on this, I decided to come back with fresh eyes, and starts again, taking the advice in the manual on weakly informative ljk priors for covariances (p, 78 of the Stan 2.9.0 reference manual). When I implement the example as is (with no hierarchies) everything runs fine (not surprisingly).
>
> So for the next stage I am trying to have a group level intercept and slope with (for now) no correlation, in essence, a SUR version of Gelman and Hill's example 17.1. When I try to run the model (as in file sur_mlm_1b) I get the warning error messages at the bottom of this page.
>
> I am not quite sure where I am going wrong. It may be something I don't understand very well about the cholesky decomposition of the covariance matrix, or it could be an even dumber coding error, but I thought I had better ask rather than beat my head against a brick wall. I do realise that the choice of priors on sigma_a and sigma_b may leave something to be desired, but I don't think that is the problem.
>
> Incidentally, although this is not the main issue I am also getting the following error sporadically when I try to run the model in rstan--it is the "Error in readRDS(file.rda) : unknown input format" which seems confusing,
>
> DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:Warning (non-fatal):
> Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
> If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
> Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
> a[k, j] ~ normal(...)
> Warning (non-fatal):
> Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
> If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
> Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
> b[k, j] ~ normal(...)
> Error in readRDS(file.rda) : unknown input format
>
> Any advice on this greatly appreciated.
>
> Lindsay
>
